% Pattern: head/item-claim. A proof states its claims as the items of a list
% with bold labels, as \item[{\bf A1.}], and proves each one after the list
% with "Proof of A1". Each item is a claim with the number of its label, and
% each proof proves the claim of its label in the same proof. An item with a
% label that no proof names is not a claim. Seen in the gold pilot (set X).
% want proposition-1 statement/proposition 1
% want proof-1 proof - proves=proposition-1
% want head-1 statement/claim A1 lines=22-22
% want head-2 statement/claim A2 lines=23-23
% want head-3 proof - proves=head-1
% want head-4 proof - proves=head-2
% want proposition-2 statement/proposition 2
% want proof-2 proof - proves=proposition-2
% want head-5 statement/claim A1 lines=33-33
% want head-6 proof - proves=head-5
\documentclass{article}
\newtheorem{proposition}{Proposition}
\begin{document}
\begin{proposition} Every compact space is bounded. \end{proposition}
\begin{proof} We show two assertions.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[{\bf A1.}\,] The space has a finite cover by balls.
\item[{\bf A2.}\,] Each ball of the cover is bounded.
\end{enumerate}

{\it Proof of \,{\bf A1}}.\, Cover the space by balls and take a finite cover.

{\it Proof of \,{\bf A2}}.\, Each ball has a finite radius.
\end{proof}
\begin{proposition} Every finite space is compact. \end{proposition}
\begin{proof} We show one assertion.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[{\bf A1.}\,] Each cover has a finite subcover.
\item[{\bf B1.}\,] The space is finite.
\end{enumerate}

{\it Proof of \,{\bf A1}}.\, Take one set of the cover for each point.
\end{proof}
\end{document}
